authentication.notes: Standard Odoo session — no custom auth module required

response_fields.uid: integer — user ID, null if auth failed

auth.login.side_effects: Sets session cookie — store in SecureStorage

errors.session_expired: HTTP 200 with error code 100 — trigger re-auth

tags.resolve.description: Find or prepare project tags by name
tags.resolve.notes: Compare returned names against mobile tags — create missing ones via tags.create

notes.pull.description: Pull the records linked on this server modified since last sync: tasks (any project) as below, and in the same way crm.lead (name, description, tag_ids, date_deadline), account.move (narration) and mail.activity (summary, note, date_deadline, active on 17+); one pull cursor per model (tasks keep the server's own); nothing linked, no request

domain: {note_links.res_id of this server's live task links}
kwargs.offset: {page * 100} — pages until fewer than 100 rows, at most 50 pages

notes.pull.notes: Filtered by linked ids, not project_id: a task created in a project, or moved to one on the server, keeps syncing. Tag names are read from project.tags / crm.tag; the note keeps the app's own tag of each name (created when missing), and pushes send the names of its tags, never the app's ids. Each row is merged into its note three ways against the link's base (note_links.params.base, the note's and the record's values at their last exchange): a field changed on the server only is copied into the note (text: the record's paragraphs replace the note's text entries, app lines and the marker skipped), except the date (date_deadline, an activity's included), kept as note_links.params.dateProposal {to} for the user to take into the note's first date entry or refuse (the base's remote date then moves to it, so that day is not proposed again), one changed in the app only waits for the push, one changed on both sides to different values is kept as note_links.params.conflict and the server turns 'conflict'. An activity archived on 17+ turns its link 'done'. A link with no base takes the server's values unless the note waits for that server. geo_task_point requires erplibre_mobile_todo installed.

notes.poll.description: Lightweight poll — fetch only IDs and write_date of the linked tasks to detect changes; no linked task, no request

domain: {note_links.res_id of this server's live task links}

notes.create.description: Push a new note to Odoo — returns the Odoo ID to store locally

args.name: {note.title}
args.project_id: {outbox.params.projectId} — the project chosen for this server, or false (personal task)
args.geo_task_point: {geojson_multipoint} — only when the note has positions and fields_get finds the field

notes.create.response: integer — Odoo task ID → stored in mobile SQLite note_links (note, server config id, project.task, id, client_uuid)
notes.create.notes: tag_ids uses Odoo ORM command 6 (replace all) on create; writes send the tags added and removed (see notes.update). The link starts with a base of the values sent. geo_task_point is GeoJSON string. Runs as the note's task.create row of sync_outbox; on a retry (attempts > 1) notes.find_created runs first. With a project, projects.check runs just before. AccessError, ValidationError, UserError or MissingError on create blocks the row as refused (no retry, createSentAt cleared since the server answered) until the user chooses again. A task deleted on the server is recreated only through the picker: choosing its project queues this create. project_id is sent by create only: notes.update never sends it.

projects.list.description: Projects offered for a new task on one server, cached in remote_records_cache (replaced on each read) for offline choices
projects.list.response: active projects the user can read; 500 rows means the list may be cut

leads.create.description: Push a note as a CRM opportunity (lead.create row of sync_outbox, same marker, retry search and quiet window as notes.create)

args.name: {note.title}
tag_ids: {crm.tag ids, found or created by name}
args.date_deadline: {first date entry, local day YYYY-MM-DD} — false when the note has no date

leads.create.response: integer — crm.lead id → note_links (note, server config id, crm.lead, id, client_uuid)
leads.create.notes: Team and salesperson are the server's defaults. done and pinned are not sent. Before create, a chosen partner is checked with res.partner search_read [('id','=',partnerId)] (active only): none or AccessError blocks the row as partner_missing. Refused create: as notes.create.

leads.update.description: Push changes to a linked opportunity

args.date_deadline: … only when the note has a date

leads.update.notes: type, partner_id, expected_revenue and active are never written: they belong to the server once created (writing active would revive an opportunity marked lost). MissingError marks the link deleted; the server leaves the note's queue only when no other kind of the note is live there. Leads are not pulled back yet; a pulled task change queues the note's opportunity on the same server.

invoices.create.description: Draft a note's invoice (invoice.create row of sync_outbox, one per note and server; same marker in narration, retry search and quiet window as notes.create)

args.partner_id: {outbox.params.partnerId} — omitted when none (allowed on a draft)

invoice_line_ids.name: {line.name}
invoice_line_ids.price_unit: {line.priceUnit} — omitted when none typed: the server computes the product's

args.{extra field}: {outbox.params.extra[field]} — each required field the form asked
args.{tie field}: {note's task or opportunity id} — when account.move has a settable many2one to it

invoices.create.notes: Before create, a chosen partner is checked (partner_missing). The tie (outbox.params.linkKind task|lead) uses the note's live link of that kind on the server; the tie field is a many2one of account.move to its model, not readonly, without depends (capabilities.probe fields). Without one, after the create, a logged note is posted on the invoice and on the task or opportunity, each linking to the other (<a data-oe-model data-oe-id>); a failure there is kept in note_links.params (crossLinked false, crossError), the invoice staying created. An invoice tied to a task or opportunity whose creation is still in the outbox waits for it (not due, not sent, a tap reports it as incomplete; depends_on set when queued after it): the tie is set at creation only. An invoice found again by its marker, or adopted, gets each cross message only when its chatter lacks it (mail.message search_count on the anchor). Refused create: as notes.create, plus builtins.ValueError and TypeError (a malformed extra value). A datetime extra value is sent as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS in UTC. tags, done, pinned, archived are not mapped.

invoices.update.description: Push changes to a note's linked invoice
invoices.update.notes: narration only: type, partner, date, reference, lines and extra fields belong to accounting once drafted. MissingError: as notes.update.

invoices.form.description: Required fields a new invoice of one type needs beyond the form's own
invoices.form.response: fields required, not readonly, with empty depends (not computed or related), absent from default_get and not the form's own (move_type, partner_id, invoice_date, ref, invoice_line_ids, line_ids, narration). char, text, integer, float, monetary, date, datetime, boolean, selection and many2one (name_search on its relation) are asked; other types are listed as unsupported. Kept per server and type in sync_target_prefs (kind invoice.form.{moveType}) for offline.

calendar.read.description: Activities of the activity calendar, per server: the connected user's and those of the users chosen, kept in activities_cache (replaced on each read, local changes still pending kept)
calendar.read.notes: A second read gets the overdue ones ([('date_deadline','<',today)], order date_deadline desc, own limit of 500), so a long backlog never hides what is coming; a read returning its limit flags the calendar as truncated. On Odoo 17+ a third read gets those done since today - 30 days: domain + [('active','=',False),('date_done','>=',…)], context active_test false, fields date_done and write_date; a done one sits on the local day of write_date (16 deletes done activities). uid comes from /web/session/get_session_info (auth user), read once per server and kept in sync_target_prefs (kind calendar.uid) to tell the user's activities apart offline. Chosen users are kept per server in sync_target_prefs (kind calendar.users); the sales team shortcut reads crm.team [('member_ids','in',[uid])] member_ids, then res.users names (none without the CRM: KeyError).

calendar.done.description: Mark an activity done from the calendar (calendar.done row of sync_outbox, note_id 'calendar')
calendar.done.notes: Applied to the cache at once (done, pending), sent at once online, else by the next sync. On 17+ the activity's active flag is read first: archived means done already, no second call. MissingError or no row drops it from the cache. A note_links row of kind activity for that id turns 'done'. A newer change of the same kind for the same activity replaces the queued one. AccessError, ValidationError or UserError is final: the operation is dropped, the cached activity back to its state before the change (kept in params.before), with the reason (lastError).

calendar.reschedule.description: Give an activity a new deadline from the calendar (calendar.reschedule row of sync_outbox, note_id 'calendar')
calendar.reschedule.notes: Same queueing as calendar.done. Once written, the deadline goes into the base (remote date) of the note link of that activity, if any: the next pull proposes nothing, and the note keeps its own date. Local reminders (hour, days before, off by default) of the user's open activities are rescheduled after each calendar read and at the app's start, from the cache.

partners.search.description: Client search for a new opportunity
partners.search.response: [[id, display_name], …] — kept in remote_records_cache (200 most recent per server) for offline search

activities.create.description: Schedule one of a note's activities on a chosen record (activity.create row of sync_outbox; a note can have several per server; same marker, retry search in note, and quiet window as notes.create)

args.date_deadline: {outbox.params.deadline} YYYY-MM-DD — none chosen: the device's day, fixed once in params.defaultDeadline

activities.create.response: integer — mail.activity id → note_links (kind activity, params_json: resModel, resId, resName, typeId, typeName, deadline, userId, userName)
activities.create.notes: res_model_id is resolved by mail.activity.default_get from default_res_model, so ir.model (admin only on 17 and 18) is never read. Before create, the record's model is probed (capabilities.probe, cached a day): missing, or without activity_ids, blocks the row as model_unusable; builtins.AttributeError on create (a model without mail.activity.mixin) blocks it as refused. Then the record (active_test false), the type and the user are each checked with search_read [('id','=',…)]: none, AccessError or KeyError (no such model) blocks the row as record_missing, type_missing or user_missing. A row without resId (chosen offline, no record in the cache) is incomplete and sends nothing. Refused create: as notes.create. The server checks the user's right on the record.

activities.update.description: Push changes to a live activity of the note
activities.update.notes: The record, type, deadline and user are create only. On Odoo 17+ the activity's active flag is read first (search_read [('id','=',…)], fields active, active_test false): archived (done on the server, its type keeping done activities) turns the link 'done' with no write; no row counts as MissingError. MissingError (the activity was done or cancelled on the server) marks the link deleted without raising; the server leaves the note's queue only when nothing else of the note lives there.

activities.done.description: The note is done: mark its live activities done
activities.done.notes: Replaces activities.update for a done note, after the same active check (an archived activity is not marked done again). The server removes the activity, or archives it when its type keeps done activities; the link turns remote_state 'done' and is never written again, even if the note is undone. An activity created for a note already done is marked done in the same push.

messages.post.description: Post a note in a chosen record's chatter (message.post row of sync_outbox; several per server; same marker, retry search and quiet window as notes.create)
messages.post.response: integer — mail.message id → note_links (kind message, params_json: resModel, resId, resName, bodyHash)
messages.post.notes: A logged note, the only kind the edit route accepts on 16. Before posting, the model is probed (missing or without message_ids: model_unusable) and the record checked (active_test false): none, AccessError or KeyError blocks as record_missing; builtins.AttributeError blocks as refused. The retry search reads mail.message [('model','=',resModel),('res_id','=',resId),('body','ilike',marker)]. Posting needs write access on most models, read on those whose _mail_post_access is read (account.move).

messages.update.description: Push a change of the note's text to its posted message
messages.update.notes: The web client's edit route (type json, auth public), on Odoo 16, 17 and 18; only the author (or an admin) of a comment without tracking may edit, and 16 only a logged note. Sent only when the body's hash differs from note_links.params.bodyHash. The message is read first through call_kw (mail.message search_read [('id','=',…)], fields body, attachment_ids): a stale session there answers code 100 and is renewed, where the public route would answer NotFound; no row, or an emptied body without attachments (deleted in the chatter), marks the link deleted; its attachment_ids are sent back, since the route replaces the list. A message found again by its marker with the hash it was posted with is linked without an edit.

activity_types.list.description: Activity types offered for a new activity, cached in remote_records_cache (replaced on each read)
activity_types.list.response: active types; a type with res_model is offered only on that model. The default deadline is the note's first date, else today plus delay_count delay_unit, as the server computes it for an activity with no previous one (whatever delay_from).

records.search.description: Record an activity goes on, or the user it is assigned to: same as partners.search, on the chosen model (res.partner, crm.lead, project.task, project.project, sale.order, account.move, purchase.order, or a technical name typed) or on res.users
records.search.response: [[id, display_name], …] — kept in remote_records_cache (200 most recent per server and model). The fixed models are probed (capabilities.probe: read right and activity_ids) and greyed where missing.

projects.check.description: Before creating a task in a project: the project still exists, is active (as projects.list offers it) and the user sees it
projects.check.response: 1 row → create; 0 rows (gone, archived, hidden) or AccessError → the outbox row turns blocked as project_missing, no create sent, sync_target_prefs stops offering that project, and the next tap asks for a project again

notes.find_created.description: Before retrying a create whose answer may have been lost: find the task an earlier attempt created, by its marker. Runs no earlier than 3 minutes after the last create was sent (stored in params.createSentAt before sending): longer than the 30 s read timeout plus Odoo's default limit_time_real (120 s), so an uncommitted create cannot be missed
notes.find_created.response: 0 rows → create; 1 row → adopt it (notes.update with the current content, then link); several rows (a copy made on the server carries the marker too, archived or not) → the outbox row turns blocked as ambiguous with the ids as candidates, and the app asks the user which task to link

capabilities.probe.description: What a server allows on a model, cached in server_capabilities; never reads ir.model (not readable by an ordinary internal user on 17 and 18)
calls: {model}.fields_get([], attributes=[type, string, required, readonly, relation, selection]) — an unknown model answers KeyError: exists=false; AccessError: exists, no right; any other error leaves the cache unchanged
Odoo 18: {model}.has_access([], 'read'|'create'|'write'); refused, or Odoo 16-17: {model}.check_access_rights('read'|'create'|'write', raise_exception=False); neither answering → null (not blocking)
activity_ids / message_ids among the fields → activities / chatter available

notes.update.description: Push changes to an existing note

args.name: {note.title}
args.description: {note.html_description} (+ the marker when the link has a client_uuid)
args.project_id: never sent: a task moved to another project on the server stays there
args.state: 1_done if note.done else 01_in_progress (Odoo 17+ only) — only when done changed in the app
args.date_deadline: {first date entry: its local day YYYY-MM-DD on Odoo 16 (Date), its UTC instant YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS on 17+ (Datetime); false for none}
args.geo_task_point: {geojson_multipoint} — only when the note has positions and fields_get finds the field

notes.update.notes: The task is read and merged first (see notes.pull); a conflict stops the push (nothing written; a background push leaves it to the user). Only the fields changed in the app since the base are sent: name (title), description (text: the user's paragraphs; media: the lines the app writes from photos, audio, video, date and position, sent but never read back) and geo_task_point, tag_ids (tags, as commands 4 and 3 so tags others set stay), date_deadline (date), state (done), active (archived), priority (pinned); none changed, no write. The same applies to crm.lead (name, description, tag_ids, date_deadline), account.move (narration for title or text) and mail.activity (summary, note; its deadline is pulled, never written). A record not read back is written in full, so the server says whether it is deleted (MissingError). A link with no base yet is written in full as before, then gets one.

attachments.list.description: List attachments for a set of tasks

attachments.upload.description: Upload a media file (audio, photo, video) as task attachment
attachments.upload.notes: Upload only on WiFi option recommended for video files. Requires valid session cookie.

chat.data.description: Load the Discuss store of the account: self partner, member channels with their last message, counters and the bus id they are as of
chat.data.response: {Store: {discuss.channel[], mail.message[], res.partner[], discuss.channel.member[], inbox: {counter_bus_id}}} — read by the app's Store parser; unknown keys are ignored
chat.data.notes: Preceded by /web/session/get_session_info for the partner id, is_system and websocket_worker_version. Counters are authoritative as of Store.inbox.counter_bus_id; a bus notification older than that mark is not applied over them. A cached channel the answer no longer lists is dropped, unless pinned locally or holding a queued post. Odoo 18 only.

chat.messages.description: One page of a channel's history

params.around: {oldest loaded message id - 1, or last message id + 1 for the first page}

chat.messages.response: {data: Store} — messages above `around` are discarded by the app, those below are upserted
chat.messages.notes: Only `around` is sent, never `before` or `after`: the answer is a window on both sides of it. A page shorter than the page size marks the history complete.

chat.post.description: Post a message in a channel; queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.post) and made idempotent

post_data.erplibre_client_uuid: {client uuid} — only when the erplibre_mobile_chat module is installed
post_data.attachment_ids: [attachment ids] — only when the message has files; the ids of the chat.upload answers, in pick order
post_data.partner_ids: [partner ids] — only when the text mentions people (the partners picked in the composer whose @Name is still in the text)
post_data.parent_id: {server id of the message answered} — only for a reply, read when the post is sent; a reply to a message still queued waits for its post

params.attachment_tokens: [false, …] — only with attachment_ids, same length: an internal user's pending attachments carry no token

chat.post.body_rules:
The body is what the browser composer of Odoo 18 posts for the same text (prettifyMessageContent of mail/static/src/utils/common/format.js): the text escaped (& < > ' " and the backtick), trimmed, a run of two line ends or more as two
, any other line end as one
, URLs as , emoji shortcodes and emoticons converted as the picker does, the first @Name of a picked person as @Name, a picked channel as an o_channel_redirect link, @everyone as a special mention. A body that starts with a mention is stored by Odoo's sanitizer wrapped in rather than

. Goldens produced by Odoo's own formatter in a headless browser pin the output byte for byte (long_test/mobile_sync_composer.py).
chat.post.response: {"mail.message": [{id, ...}], ...Store} — the id settles the pending bubble; an answer without an id is an error and the retry searches before posting
chat.post.idempotency: Every body ends with the hidden comment `<!-- erplibre-mobile:<uuid> -->`; with the module the uuid also travels in the field `erplibre_client_uuid` of mail.message. A send stamps createSentAt; a retry first waits out the quiet window (3 minutes), then runs mail.message search_read [model = discuss.channel, res_id = channel, author_id = the session partner, body ilike the marker] with limit 2, keeps the hits whose body holds the exact comment, and adopts the one found instead of posting again. Two hits block the op as ambiguous. Search by author, so another member's message that quotes the uuid is never taken for the post.
chat.post.notes: A reply whose parent the server drops answers parentMessage false: the message stays a plain message, no error; a post found again after a lost answer reads parent_id from the server. A channel mention (#) notifies only a partner with an email address and inbox notifications. Posts of one channel go out in order: each op depends on the previous unfinished one, so a failed post holds the ones after it. AccessError, ValidationError, UserError, MissingError, NotFound and Forbidden mark the bubble failed and block the op; anything else retries (30 s doubled per attempt, 1 h max). After a post the channel is marked read for its author unless a newer message is known. With files: the post waits until every file of the message is uploaded; a refused file is left out; with no text and no file left the message fails. A refusal of the post, before any re-upload, asks the server which attachment ids it still holds (ir.attachment search_read on the ids) and uploads the missing ones again once.

chat.upload.description: Upload one file of a message as a pending attachment of a channel (no message yet); queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.upload, one lane apart from the posts) and sent by the native layer as a streamed multipart request

request_fields.csrf_token: {token of chat.csrf} — required by both routes
request_fields.is_pending: true — the attachment is created on mail.compose.message / res_id 0 until a post claims it
request_fields.voice: true — only for a voice file; Odoo reads any value as true
request_fields.client_uuid: {local uuid of the file} — module route only

chat.upload.response: {"data": Store} — the ir.attachment record is in data["ir.attachment"]; {"error": text} is a refusal (not allowed to upload there)
chat.upload.idempotency: On the module route a request repeating the client_uuid of the same user returns the attachment already created, without a second one and without replaying the voice metadata, even if the thread or the file differ (unique index on create_uid + erplibre_client_uuid, advisory lock per uuid). The module route also keeps the original of an image (image_no_postprocess), where Odoo's route reduces it on save. Only an internal user is served: the public user (expired session) and a portal user read 404; a missing client_uuid reads 400. On Odoo's route nothing makes the upload idempotent: a retry after a lost answer first searches (chat.upload_find), and a retry that finds nothing sends again.
chat.upload.notes: The body is a one-shot stream: the transfer is never resent by the HTTP stack, a retry is the outbox's. A first 404, or a 400 whose text names the CSRF token, forgets the token and re-authenticates once (callWithAuth), then calls again with a new session and token; a second 404 refuses the file for good (not_found). 413 refuses it as too big. Any other 400 retries later: a retry overlapping the first request on the module route meets the unique index and answers 400, and the next retry finds the attachment. The size limit is session_info max_file_upload_size; a file fits when its size + 65536 bytes of envelope does not exceed it. A file is uploaded after its predecessor of the same post and before the post.

chat.csrf.description: Read the CSRF token the upload routes require
chat.csrf.request: Cookie session_id only, no redirect parameter: the login page is rendered, with its token, even for a logged-in session
chat.csrf.response: HTML — the token is the value of the hidden input csrf_token, else the csrf_token of the layout's odoo object
chat.csrf.notes: No JSON route returns the token. It derives from the session id: one fetch per session, shared by concurrent requests, forgotten when the server refuses it, never reused for a new session. A 3xx answer (session gone, or a database selector) is SessionExpiredError and the call re-authenticates once; another non-2xx or a page without a token is an error to retry later.

chat.upload_find.description: Look for the pending attachment of an upload whose answer was lost, on Odoo's route

args: {size} — left out for png, jpeg, bmp and tiff
{upload sent at minus a clock skew}
{upload ended at, or now, plus a clock skew}

kwargs.limit: 1 + the number of attachment ids this phone already holds for the account

chat.upload_find.notes: Runs before a repeated upload once the quiet window of the first send is over. Odoo's route resizes and re-encodes png, jpeg, bmp and tiff past 1920 px (ir.attachment._postprocess_contents, base.image_autoresize_extensions), so their stored size is not the size sent and the size term is left out for them. Uploads this search cannot tell apart (the same name, and the same size unless either one is png, jpeg, bmp or tiff) are ordered by the phone, one at a time: two of them are never in doubt at once. The hits the phone already holds (state uploaded) are dropped, the oldest left is adopted. Not used on the module route, which answers the repeat itself.

chat.attachment_preview.description: Download the preview of an image or video attachment
chat.attachment_preview.response: the image resized to 512x512 at most, written to the cache directory of the phone
chat.attachment_preview.notes: Previews download whatever the network. `unique` busts Odoo's cache when the file changes; `download=true` turns an error into a 404 instead of a placeholder image. The session cookie is sent; a 404 reads as an expired session and re-authenticates once.

chat.attachment_download.description: Download the original of an attachment, to the cache or to open it
chat.attachment_download.response: the file, streamed by the native layer to its path under Directory.Data
chat.attachment_download.notes: Starts when the user opens the file (or taps to download). With « Wi-Fi only » on and the phone off Wi-Fi, the original (a voice message included) waits for Wi-Fi, and « download anyway » takes that one file now; previews never wait. The route is auth=public: an expired session reads 404, handled as for chat.upload.

chat.attachment_delete_bus.description: Bus notification that an attachment was deleted on the server
chat.attachment_delete_bus.notes: The phone removes the row and its cached files, the thumbnail and the original, and refreshes the conversation.

chat.reaction.description: Add or remove the user's reaction to a message; queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.reaction) as a target state per message and emoji

params.content: {emoji, the exact string: U+2764 U+FE0F for the heart}
params.action: add | remove — always explicit, never a toggle

chat.reaction.response: {"mail.message": [{id, reactions}], "MessageReactions": [{content, count, sequence, personas, message}], ...Store}. When reactions remain, reactions is [["ADD", [{message, content}]]] and personas lists the whole group each time. When the last one is removed, reactions is [["DELETE", {message, content}]]: the DELETE value is a single object, not a list, and the parser accepts both forms.
chat.reaction.idempotency: The route is idempotent per action: adding a reaction already held, or removing one not held, changes nothing. The outbox keeps one op per (message, emoji) holding the last wanted action and the state the server held when it was first queued (base); a state equal to base cancels the op before it is sent, so no request goes out. An op that may have been sent (sentAt) is never cancelled, a toggle back after a lost answer is sent. A reaction on a message still queued depends on its post and resolves the message by the post's client uuid.
chat.reaction.notes: A message that no longer exists (MissingError, NotFound) drops the op with a notice and shows the reaction as the server held it. Reactions create no notification. Deleting a message does not remove its reactions, which the thread hides with the message.

chat.edit.description: Edit the body of the user's own message; queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.edit), refused rather than overwriting a message that changed

params.partner_ids: [partner ids of the mentions in the body]
params.attachment_ids: null — the attachments stay (both routes treat null as unchanged); [] removes them all
params.expected_fingerprint: {sha256 hex of the UTF-8 body as Store returned it; empty or false reads as the empty string} — module route only

chat.edit.response: Odoo's own answer (a Store holding the message). The module route answers {"erplibre_conflict": "changed" | "deleted", ...Store of the message as it is} and writes nothing when the fingerprint differs from the message's erplibre_body_fingerprint, or when an emptied message would receive a non-empty body (deleted).
chat.edit.idempotency: A route is chosen by the module level 1.3 (field erplibre_body_fingerprint on mail.message, readable by any user). With it, the fingerprint of the body the edit was made against (baseBody) is sent and the route locks the row (SELECT … FOR UPDATE, after the access checks) before comparing, so two concurrent edits cannot both pass; the loser fails in serialization and Odoo replays the request. Without it, the app re-reads body and attachments just before Odoo's route and refuses an emptied message (deleted) or a body other than baseBody (changed). In both cases a server body that reads as the text this edit sends (the edited span, the paragraph and sanitizer wrapping ignored) counts as this edit already written, an answer lost: the op is done without a write.
chat.edit.notes: Only an internal user is served by the module route; a non-numeric message_id, a missing or unreadable message or one the user may not edit reads 404 without taking the lock. A plain 404 of the module route probes the module and retries on the route the probe leaves. A refused edit keeps its text: the notice offers « Reprendre », which puts the text back in the composer (as a new message when the original was deleted). The edited message shows « (modifié) » from the span o-mail-Message-edited Odoo adds to the stored body. Editing a message still queued rewrites its post and sends no update. A mention added by an edit notifies no one (Odoo's behaviour).

chat.delete.description: Delete the user's own message, as Odoo's Discuss does: an edit that empties it; queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.delete)
chat.delete.response: Odoo's own answer; the message stays on the server with an empty body and no attachment, and the bus event mail.record/insert tells the other clients.
chat.delete.idempotency: Replaying an emptying leaves the message empty. A delete meeting a message already empty, or a vanished one, counts as done. Deleting a message still queued cancels its post and its uploads.
chat.delete.notes: The thread hides a message with no text and no file, and a reply quoting it shows « message d'origine supprimé ». Its reactions are kept by the server and hidden with it.

chat.mention_suggestions.description: People and channels offered while typing @ or # in the composer
chat.mention_suggestions.response: @: a Store of the matching members and users of the channel (res.partner records). #: a list of channel rows.
chat.mention_suggestions.notes: Online only: offline, or after a request that was not sent, the suggestions come from the cached members (and the people cache in a public channel). In a chat, a group and a restricted channel the @ list offers members only, as the browser does. Never blocks typing.

chat.message_delete_bus.description: Bus notification that messages were deleted on the server
chat.message_delete_bus.notes: Sent by mail.message.unlink to the partners it notified; a delete made in Discuss is an emptying edit and arrives as mail.record/insert instead. The phone removes the rows it holds and refreshes the conversation.

chat.read.description: Mark a channel read up to its last known message; queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.read), one op per channel whose message id only rises
chat.read.notes: When the channel has mentions, mail.message mark_all_as_read via /web/dataset/call_kw with args [[[model = discuss.channel], [res_id = channel id]]] follows. A refused error is swallowed: a channel the user cannot reach any more has nothing left to mark. With the option to send read receipts off, nothing is sent. Local counters change only when the server reports them back (/mail/data or the bus).

chat.typing.notes: Sent only online, with the option on and in a channel the user is a member of (Odoo would make them one). true at most once per 50 s while keystrokes continue; false 5 s after the last keystroke, or at once on an explicit stop, and only after a true. A failed call is dropped.

chat.fetched.description: Tell a direct chat its messages were delivered to this device
chat.fetched.notes: Only for channels of type chat, after a read; a courtesy whose failure is ignored.

chat.create_dm.description: Open or create the direct message with one person; queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.create, mode dm)
chat.create_dm.response: {Store} with the discuss.channel — its id replaces the temporary id the conversation was shown under
chat.create_dm.notes: Odoo returns the existing chat, so a repeat is safe and no uuid is needed. The conversation is cached at once under a temporary negative channel id (the negative of the clock in ms), with placeholder members (self, then the person), and the pair is kept in chat_temp_ids when the real id arrives. Showing a hidden direct message again queues the same op on its real id and cancels a hide still waiting. Refused errors (AccessError, ValidationError, UserError, MissingError, NotFound, Forbidden) give the op up as a notice blocked in the outbox until dismissed; anything else retries (30 s doubled per attempt, 1 h max).

chat.create_group.description: Create a group of people; queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.create, mode group)

context.erplibre_client_uuid: {op client uuid} — only when the module 1.1 is installed (state installed, option chat module mode auto); an outdated module (1.0) creates without it

chat.create_group.idempotency: With the module 1.1 the server creates one group per (create_uid, erplibre_client_uuid): an advisory transaction lock serialises two requests, a partial unique index guarantees, and the repeat gets the first group back. Without it, a send stamps createSentAt; a retry first waits out the quiet window (3 minutes), then searches discuss.channel [create_uid = uid, channel_type = group, create_date within createSentAt - 5 min and createSentAt + quiet window + 5 min, is_member, name = the op's name when it has one], drops the conversations another create of this phone already settled on, keeps those whose members are exactly the op's people plus self, and adopts the one found (read through /discuss/channel/info). Two matches block the op as ambiguous.
chat.create_group.notes: Cached at once under a temporary negative channel id with placeholder members, so a group without a name shows their names. A refusal marks the cached conversation create_failed (kept until dismissed) and cancels the op and what waits for it. Refused errors (AccessError, ValidationError, UserError, MissingError, NotFound, Forbidden) give the op up as a notice blocked in the outbox until dismissed; anything else retries (30 s doubled per attempt, 1 h max).

chat.create_channel.description: Create a channel restricted to an access group or open to everyone; queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.create, mode channel)

context.erplibre_client_uuid: {op client uuid} — only when the module 1.1 is installed (state installed, option chat module mode auto)

chat.create_channel.idempotency: As chat.create_group: the module 1.1 dedupes by (create_uid, erplibre_client_uuid); without it the fingerprint search runs on channel_type = channel and the name, with no member check.
chat.create_channel.notes: The access groups offered come from chat.access_groups. Refused errors (AccessError, ValidationError, UserError, MissingError, NotFound, Forbidden) give the op up as a notice blocked in the outbox until dismissed; anything else retries (30 s doubled per attempt, 1 h max).

chat.join.description: Join a public channel; queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.join)
chat.join.notes: Adds self only when missing, so a repeat is safe. The cached row (written from the channel's name when missing) turns member at once and carries the op as create_op_id, so posts written meanwhile wait for the join. A channel the user cannot reach gives the join up like a refused create.

chat.invite.description: Add people to a group or channel; queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.invite)
chat.invite.notes: Sent only for a member of a real conversation (a chat takes a new group instead). A conversation gone, created on the phone only, refused or no longer the user's gives the op up as vanished. Refused errors (AccessError, ValidationError, UserError, MissingError, NotFound, Forbidden) give the op up as a notice blocked in the outbox until dismissed; anything else retries (30 s doubled per attempt, 1 h max).

chat.rename.description: Rename a group or channel, or give a direct message the user's own label; queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.rename)
chat.rename.notes: channel_set_custom_name for channel_type chat, channel_rename otherwise. A target state: a later rename of the same conversation replaces a waiting one, and the value sent is the last one written into the op. Refused errors (AccessError, ValidationError, UserError, MissingError, NotFound, Forbidden) give the op up as a notice blocked in the outbox until dismissed; anything else retries (30 s doubled per attempt, 1 h max).

chat.describe.description: Set the description of a channel; queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.describe)

chat.leave.description: Leave a conversation; queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.leave)
chat.leave.notes: The conversation turns non-member at once. Posts, renames, invites and mutes still queued for it are dropped (a post's bubble fails), and a conversation left while its create is queued is left right after the create runs. A create given up while the user leaves does not block: the channel is flagged left_unsent and the leave runs. A refused leave clears left_unsent, so the next load shows the membership the server kept. Refused errors (AccessError, ValidationError, UserError, MissingError, NotFound, Forbidden) give the op up as a notice blocked in the outbox until dismissed; anything else retries (30 s doubled per attempt, 1 h max).

chat.hide.description: Hide a direct message (unpin it on the server); queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.hide)
chat.hide.notes: The row stays cached as is_pinned = 0 and is not listed. A load keeps it hidden unless the server says it is pinned again; a new message, announced by the bus, shows it again. Showing it from the new conversation screen queues chat.create on its real id and cancels a hide still waiting.

chat.mute.description: Mute a conversation for a duration, for good, or turn the mute off; queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.mute)

params.minutes: {minutes | -1 for good | false for no mute}

chat.mute.notes: The op stores an absolute end (an ISO date, "forever" or null); the minutes are computed when the request leaves, rounded up, so a mute queued past its end sends false and unmutes. The offered durations are 15 min, 1 h, 3 h, 8 h, 24 h and for good. The route would join a non-member, so it is sent only for a member.

chat.global_mute.description: Mute every conversation of the account, or turn it off; queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.global_mute)

params.minutes: {minutes | -1 for good | false for no mute}

chat.global_mute.notes: As chat.mute without channel_id, set from Options › Chat per server. The state is read from Store.settings.mute_until_dt of /web/session/get_session_info (fresh at each load) and from the bus; chat_sources.global_mute_at keeps when the phone last wrote it, so a load that began earlier does not overwrite a newer change.

chat.remove.description: Remove another member from a group or channel; queued in sync_outbox (kind chat.remove); administrators only
chat.remove.notes: A method of the erplibre_mobile_chat module 1.1: AccessError unless the caller is a system user, UserError for a chat or a person who is not a member. Goes through Odoo's own leave path, so the removed person receives discuss.channel/leave on the bus and the thread says they left. An older or missing module answers AttributeError: the op is given up as refused and the module state is probed again. Offered only to a system user on a server whose module is installed. The member row is dropped locally when the call succeeds.

chat.members.description: Members of a conversation, page by page
chat.members.response: {Store} with discuss.channel.member and res.partner rows not in known_member_ids, at most 100, and the channel's member_count
chat.members.notes: Repeated until the cache holds member_count members or a page brings nobody new. The placeholder members written for a conversation created offline (negative ids) give way to the server's. Offline, or for a conversation only the phone knows, the cached members answer.

chat.people.description: Internal users to start a conversation with, by name
chat.people.response: {Store} of res.partner rows (the caller is never returned), merged into chat_partners
chat.people.notes: Offline, or when the request never left, the cached partners whose name contains the term (case and accents ignored) answer instead, the correspondents of recent chats first.

chat.joinable.description: Public channels the user can join
chat.joinable.response: [{id, name, description, member_count, group_public_id: [id, full name] | false}]
chat.joinable.notes: Not cached: the user is not a member, so none is a conversation yet. Offline: none, flagged offline.

chat.invite_candidates.description: People who can be added to a channel
chat.invite_candidates.response: {count, data: Store} — count is the number of matches on the server, which may exceed the partners returned; the partners are merged into chat_partners
chat.invite_candidates.notes: Name or email contains the term, not members yet, and in the channel's group when it has one. Offline: none, flagged offline.

chat.access_groups.description: Access groups a new channel can be restricted to
chat.access_groups.notes: The user's own non-portal groups by full name, then « everyone » (group id false) last. The default, the internal users group, comes from Store.internalUserGroupId (kept in chat_sources.internal_user_group_id) and is offered first even if the search does not list it. Offline: that default, when known, and everyone.

chat.websocket.description: Odoo 18 bus over a websocket: messages, counters, typing and presence in real time
chat.websocket.response: JSON arrays of notifications [{id, type, payload}] — each frame is applied, then its highest id saved

close_codes.other: exponential backoff, 1 s doubled up to 120 s plus up to 30 s of jitter, reset after a connection open for 60 s

chat.websocket.notes: Member channels are implicit in the subscription. last=0 only replays about the last 50 s, so with no saved id a store loaded longer ago than that is reloaded first; a saved id seen more than 24 h ago is stale (the server's rows are gone) and also reloads, then subscribes from 0. A ws:// address follows the same rule as http://. Keepalive every 60 s is the transport's.

chat.module.description: State of the optional erplibre_mobile_chat module; installed from the app by a system user
chat.module.notes: installed = discuss.channel holds the field erplibre_client_uuid in fields_get (module 1.1; readable by any user; cached) or a system user sees the row installed; outdated = only mail.message holds it (module 1.0) or a system user sees the row « to upgrade » (button_immediate_upgrade, offered to a system user, probed fresh afterwards like an install); available / absent = a system user sees the row not installed / no row; unknown = not a system user or offline without a cached capability. Installing calls ir.module.module button_immediate_install [[id]]; a response lost to a timeout is not a failure, the probe tells the outcome, and an AccessError returns the probed state. Without the module the app posts with the marker alone and finds a lost create by fingerprint; creates carry the uuid in the context only when installed (an outdated 1.0 takes the fingerprint path), message posts carry it for installed and outdated alike, and chat.remove needs the 1.1. Module 1.2 is recognised by erplibre_client_uuid on ir.attachment (level 1.2, above 1.1 on discuss.channel and 1.0 on mail.message); it adds the idempotent upload route of chat.upload. Module 1.3 is recognised by erplibre_body_fingerprint on mail.message (level 1.3); it adds the guarded edit route of chat.edit. Without it, files go to Odoo's route and a lost answer is found with chat.upload_find.

attachments.create: ir.attachment create {name (file name), datas (base64), res_model, res_id, mimetype} for each photo, audio or video entry with a file not sent yet to that record, after each create or write of the note's task, opportunity or invoice (on it) and of each of its messages (on the message's record, then /mail/message/update_content with the message's attachment_ids plus the new ones). Activities take none.
attachments.limits: Options › Odoo sync (localStorage options.sync.attachments): wifiOnly holds files on a mobile network (the server stays pending until a push on Wi-Fi); maxMb, and always 90 MB (base64 must stay under the server's request limit), leave a larger file out. note_links.params.attachments maps entry id → {id, path}: each file goes once per record, a replaced one (another path) again, a removed one stays on the server; a file already sent to the same record by another link of the note is reused. params.attachmentsSkipped notes a file too big, missing or refused (the round goes on), named on the note until sent, as are the files held for Wi-Fi while off it; going onto Wi-Fi from another link syncs the servers with due work, retry delays kept; params.attachmentsInFlight marks a create sent, so an unanswered one is looked for first (ir.attachment search on res_model, res_id, name); params.attachmentsUnlinked keeps ids a message could not take yet. Never fails the push.
attachments.paths: An entry's file is read through Filesystem: a web view URL (http://localhost/_capacitor_file_/…) as its native file, an absolute path or file:// as is, a relative path (a recording) under Directory.Data.

companies.read: /web/session/get_session_info (auth user): uid and user_companies (current_company, allowed_companies id → {id, name}); kept per server in sync_target_prefs (kind companies), the one last chosen in kind company.
companies.refresh: The kept list is read again from the session once per app run, so a company the user lost is no longer sent.
companies.scope: For a user of several companies, every call_kw to that server carries context allowed_company_ids = all of them (current first) unless the call names its own, so records of each company are read and written. A creation carries the company chosen in the picker first (outbox params.companyId), the one the record is created in. A user of one company gets no such context.

transport_policy.http: An http:// url is refused before any request (InsecureHttpError) unless the user turned on « Autoriser http (non chiffré) » in Options › Synchronisation Odoo (localStorage options.sync.allowHttp). The same rule refuses opening an application or a note's record in the web view, whose login script types the password. https is always allowed.

re_auth_strategy.trigger: JSON-RPC error code 100 (session expired) or HTTP 401 — never the error message text
steps: 3. Store new session cookie in SecureStorage key 'odoo_sync_session_{base64(app_url|username|database)}'
5. If still failing — mark this server 'error' in sync_per_server_status (the note's sync_status is derived), notify user

sync_status_values.notes: Per server in sync_per_server_status (synced | pending | error | conflict); the note's sync_status is derived from the entries of live applications: conflict, then error, then pending, then synced; none left → synced if a live link remains, else local.
sync_status_values.local: Note bound to no live server
sync_status_values.pending: Some server still has to receive the note (queued offline, edited, or edited during its push); syncAll pushes it
sync_status_values.synced: Every live server received the latest pushed content
sync_status_values.conflict: A record of the note changed in the app and on the server, the same field to different values (note_links.params.conflict: per field mine and theirs). Nothing is pushed there and syncAll skips the note until the user keeps, per field, the app's version (sent by the next push) or the server's (copied into the note).
sync_status_values.error: Last push to some server failed; syncAll retries it
sync_status_values.remote_deleted: Not a status: a write() answering odoo.exceptions.MissingError marks the note_links row remote_state='deleted'; the server leaves the note's queue only when no other kind of the note is live there (a background push next to a live kind skips the deleted one). The record is recreated only when the user chooses it again in the picker; unchecking it there marks the link 'dismissed': kept as history, never pushed nor asked again

columns.odoo_id: INTEGER — legacy single binding, no longer written; migration 2026102201 copies it to note_links
columns.sync_status: TEXT DEFAULT 'local' — see sync_status_values; derived from sync_per_server_status
columns.last_synced_at: TEXT — ISO 8601 datetime of last successful sync

note_links.notes: One row per remote record of a note; an id is only valid for its config id, which includes the database. kind 'create': the note's task or opportunity, one per model and server; kind 'activity': a mail.activity, several per server, its choices in params_json; kind 'message': a mail.message posted in a record's chatter, several per server, its record and bodyHash in params_json; remote_state 'done': an activity the app marked done. Sync config ids, per-server status keys and remembered selections all use url|username|database (migration 2026102201 upgrades the older url|username ids).

sync_pull_cursors.notes: Highest task write_date already pulled; next pull starts there (>=). Pages by write_date >= last read, excluding the ids already read at it (search_read truncates write_date to the second). Without a cursor: one day before the oldest link's last sync (device clock vs server clock).

sync_outbox.notes: One row per operation of a note on one server. attempts and running are stored before the server is contacted; success deletes the row; failure retries after 30 s doubled per attempt (1 h max); a handler may postpone a row to params.notBefore without counting an attempt, honoured even by a forced sync; blocked and incomplete wait for the user; running rows of a killed app turn failed at startup.

server_capabilities.notes: Result of capabilities.probe per server and model, used offline; probed again after one day when online.

remote_records_cache.notes: Records of a server kept for offline choices. projects.list replaces the project rows of that server as a whole; partners.search adds or refreshes the partners found and keeps the 200 most recently fetched per server.

activities_cache.notes: The activity calendar's activities per server (see calendar.read): record, type, summary, deadline, user, done/dateDone, pending (a local change waiting in the outbox).

sync_target_prefs.notes: invoice.form.out_invoice / invoice.form.in_invoice: the extra required fields of invoices.form, kept for offline. Last choice per server and kind of target (task.create: projectId, projectName), offered first; also the project of a creation queued without a choice. Kind targets: the target kinds last checked in the picker for that server (task, lead), checked by default for a note with nothing there. A lead's client and revenue are not remembered.

columns: is_pinned (migration 2026102601; 0 for a hidden direct message)
create_op_id (2026102601; the queued create or join the row waits for)
create_failed (migration 2026102602; a refused create, kept until dismissed)
left_unsent (migration 2026102603; left while texts were still queued)
chat_channels.notes: One row per conversation. The two *_bus_id columns are the bus id each counter is as of: a bus notification with a lower id does not overwrite it. oldest_loaded_id and history_complete drive history paging (chat.messages); local_pinned keeps a conversation the server stopped listing. Index idx_chat_channels_cfg. A conversation created on the phone has a negative temporary id until chat.create settles it.

columns: parent_id (migration 2026102607; the server id of the message answered)
parent_client_uuid (2026102607; the answered message while it is still queued)
recipient_ids (2026102607; JSON list of the partners mentioned)
chat_messages.notes: A queued post is stored as a pending row before any request, settled with its server id by chat.post. Indexes chat_messages_channel and idx_chat_messages_cfg (config_id, channel_id).

chat_members.notes: discuss.channel.member rows: read and delivery marks of each member, and who is typing.

chat_partners.notes: Authors and correspondents named by the Store.

columns: global_mute_until (2026102601; end of the account-wide mute)
global_mute_at (2026102601; when the phone last wrote it)
file_dir (2026102604; directory of the cached files of the server)
chat_sources.notes: One row per server: the session facts, the last bus id applied and when it was seen, the module state (installed|outdated|available|absent|unknown), the bus id the inbox counter is as of, the default access group of new channels and the account-wide mute.

chat_temp_ids.notes: The server id each conversation created on the phone was given, by its temporary id: a screen or route still naming the temporary id finds the conversation, and a fingerprint search never adopts a conversation another create already took.

columns: origin (migration 2026102606; where a draft file was taken: camera, gallery, file, voice)
chat_attachments.notes: One row per file of a message. The paths and byte counts describe the files cached on the phone; the purge (off by default, 2048 MB, a warning at 80 %) deletes the oldest-opened cached files and keeps the row.

columns: reply_to (migration 2026102608; JSON target of the message answered)
edit_of (2026102608; JSON target of the message being edited)
mentions (2026102608; JSON people and channels picked in either text)
chat_drafts.notes: One draft text per conversation, kept across restarts. The reply target, the edit in progress and the mention picks are kept with it. Its files are the conversation's chat_attachments rows in the draft state.

columns: message_key (m{message id}, or u{client uuid} for a message still queued)
partner_ids (JSON list in the server's order)
chat_reactions.notes: One row per reaction group of a message; guests are only counted. Index chat_reactions_channel (config_id, channel_id). Migrations 2026102607 (reactions, chat_messages.parent_id, parent_client_uuid and recipient_ids) and 2026102608 (chat_drafts reply, edit and mentions) add columns only when PRAGMA table_info does not list them, so a fresh install and a second run change nothing.
